field_evidence_note: Each index names the dossier evidence item that actually supports the canonical field; the promotion step emits one formal evidence row per field/index pair.
limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No crafted RAR archive, OSS-Fuzz harness, or upstream regression test was executed; the finding is static.
The amount of adjacent memory disclosed by the over-read depends on allocator layout and was not measured.

The same fix commit also corrects the second memcpy destination from buffer to buffer + firstpart, which is a distinct write-side bug at the same line; this dossier's canonical description follows the CVE's over-read wording but records both changes.

NVD has no Primary metric for this CVE: both entries (Red Hat and nvd@nist.gov) are marked Secondary and carry the same 6.6 vector; the canonical severity therefore has only one numeric value, not two independent assessments.
Only the upstream 3.8.0 fix was verified; the Red Hat errata backports (RHSA-2025:21885 and later) were not diffed.

The independent reviewer classified the defect technically as CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read) because the ASan report is a READ and CVSS integrity impact is N; the CNA and NVD records assign CWE-122. The formal cwe_ids keep CWE-122 as the authoritative assignment and record the CWE-125 analysis here rather than overriding the CNA.
Red Hat's own severity rating is Low while its CVSS vector computes 6.6 Medium; the formal severity uses the numeric vector as published and does not reinterpret the rating.

v3.7.7 is on the 3.7.x maintenance branch and is not an ancestor of v3.8.0. The OSV linear GIT range (introduced 0, fixed at the v3.8.0 release commit) therefore does not cover v3.7.6-v3.7.9; the version-based CNA/CPE range <3.8.0 does, and all four 3.7.x tags were confirmed to lack the fix.

critical_operation.description: copy_from_lzss_window() copies `length` bytes out of the LZSS window into the VM buffer. parse_filter() (lines 3264-3267) accepts a filter blocklength from the RAR bitstream without comparing it with rar->dictionary_size, and run_filters() (line 3429) only checks it against VM_MEMORY_SIZE. When blocklength exceeds the window size, firstpart is smaller than length and the line 3114 memcpy reads `length - firstpart` bytes from window[0], past the end of the allocated LZSS window. The fix adds `if (blocklength > rar->dictionary_size) return 0;` in parse_filter and also corrects this memcpy's destination to buffer + firstpart.

entry_point.description: Extracting an attacker-supplied RAR archive reaches expand(), which calls read_filter() at line 2965. read_filter() decodes the filter code block and calls parse_filter() at line 3628; the resulting filter is later executed by run_filters(), which calls copy_from_lzss_window() at line 3435 with the unchecked blocklength.

parse_filter accepts blocklength without a dictionary_size bound

location.verification_method: Static read of archive_read_support_format_rar.c at v3.7.7 and v3.8.0, the fix diff and the regression test; no archive was processed.

open_questions: Whether every RAR compression method can reach parse_filter with an attacker-controlled blocklength was not exhaustively traced; the code path is shared by the RAR reader.
The exact allocation size of the LZSS window relative to dictionary_size was not instrumented; the over-read follows from the missing bound, not from a measured run.
Whether distributions' backports introduce equivalent bounds checks was not verified beyond the upstream commit.
prepared_by: Codex collecting agent (single reviewer); no independent reviewer assigned

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read rar.c at v3.7.7 and confirm parse_filter lacks a dictionary_size bound and copy_from_lzss_window line 3114 can read past the window.
An independent reviewer must confirm the annotated tags peel to b439d586 (v3.7.7) and 70ff28fc (v3.8.0) and that a612bf62 is in 3.8.0 but not 3.7.7.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

source_crosscheck.notes: Red Hat is the CNA: its CVE v5 record supplies the <3.8.0 range, CWE-122 and CVSS 6.6 (AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:H). NVD carries two metric entries, both marked Secondary (Red Hat and nvd@nist.gov), with the identical vector; there is no NVD Primary assessment. NVD's CPE range is versionEndExcluding 3.8.0, matching the CNA. OSV converts the CPE range to a GIT range fixed at the v3.8.0 commit 70ff28fc; that commit is the release commit, not the source fix a612bf62, and because v3.7.7 diverges from the 3.8.0 branch the linear GIT range omits the 3.7.x line. OSV's version list also stops at v3.7.5. The tag check confirms v3.7.6-v3.7.9 all contain the vulnerable code and lack the fix. The CNA assigns CWE-122 (heap buffer overflow) although the reported access is a read with no integrity impact, which would technically be CWE-125; CWE-122 is kept as the authoritative assignment with the disagreement recorded.
